title: The circular economy

draft.title: The circular economy
card: Materials are taken from nature, made into products, used and then thrown away. This is often called make, use, dispose.
Waste is designed out from the start. Products and materials stay in use for as long as possible, so less new material is taken and less waste is made.
Three ways to keep materials in use are reuse (using an item again), repair (fixing it so it lasts longer) and recycling (breaking it down to make new items).
Design matters. A phone with a replaceable battery or a bottle made of one easily recycled material is easier to keep in use than one that must be thrown out when a part fails.
draft.remember: A circular economy keeps materials in use instead of throwing them away.

a.q: Which description best fits a circular economy?
opts: Products are designed so materials stay in use longer
Products are made cheaply and replaced when they break
Waste is made as usual, then buried in well-run landfills
Products are made, used once and then sent to be dumped
a.why: A circular economy designs waste out so materials keep being used through reuse, repair and recycling. Burying waste in landfill, even well run, still treats materials as something to throw away, which is the linear pattern.
a.clue: Look for the option that keeps materials in use.

b.q: Sam's company in Newcastle sells laptops with parts that can be swapped, and fixes and resells returned units. Which part of this is a circular economy action?
opts: Selling laptops at a lower price than rivals
Sending broken laptops to a dump after one year
Making a new laptop model every few months
b.why: Repairing and reselling returned laptops keeps them in use longer, so less new material is needed. A lower price does not change what happens to materials, so it is not a circular action.
b.clue: Which action keeps an existing product in use?

a.best: Products are designed so materials stay in use longer

check.summary: Two problems. The clue for question a almost repeats the right option. The stem of question b asks which 'part of this' is circular, but three options are not things Sam's company does.
